requirements.text: The assistant must answer support analysts' product questions using the organization's own product knowledge.
The application must provide a chat interface in which a support analyst converses with the assistant.
The application must keep a reviewable history of every conversation held with the assistant.
Analysts must be able to open and review past conversations so that good answers can be reused.
The assistant must identify itself clearly as automated so customers know the reply was machine-generated.
Conversation records must be stored durably so they can be retrieved for quality review.
Each question must be routed to the assistant first, and the analyst must explicitly approve the assistant's draft reply before it is sent.

Conversations and their individual messages (role, content, timestamp) must be persisted as structured records rather than opaque transcript blobs, so history can be listed, opened, and reviewed message by message.
Analysts must be able to search and filter past conversations by keyword, since the current process is manual searching of old threads.
Each draft reply must record its approval state plus the approving analyst and timestamp, so quality review can distinguish approved/sent replies from unapproved drafts.
The approval step must be part of the analyst-facing UI: the analyst can view, edit, approve, or reject the assistant's draft before it leaves the system.
The assistant must ground its answers in retrieved product-knowledge content and surface which sources it used, so the analyst can verify the draft before approving it.
The assistant must have defined behavior for questions it cannot answer from available knowledge: state that it does not know and escalate to the analyst rather than guess.
Reusing a past answer must be a supported action: an analyst reviewing a prior conversation can carry that answer into the current draft.
Stored conversation history must be readable only by authenticated support staff and must not be exposed publicly or to unauthenticated callers.
Model and knowledge-source credentials must be supplied through environment configuration and must never be committed to the repository or written into conversation records.
The application must run locally via a single container-compose command; no cloud infrastructure is required for v1 (declared deploy target is local).
The assistant must be covered by automated evaluations — at minimum self-identification as automated and refusal to answer beyond available knowledge — so behavior can be checked before release.
The application is scoped as an internal single-team tool for support analysts at low concurrency; there is no customer-facing self-service portal in v1.
The authoritative source of 'our product knowledge' and how it is kept current is unspecified: documents loaded into the application versus an existing external knowledge base the app must query.
Analyst authentication and identity are unspecified: whether analysts sign in at all, and if so via local accounts or company SSO.
The retention period for stored conversation records is unspecified.
Delivery of an approved reply is unspecified: whether the application sends it to the customer through an email/ticketing integration or the analyst copies it into the existing ticket tool.
